Ten comments

Miss McDonald

A 4-part reel that’s not heard that often. I can’t remember where it came from, but it has been recorded by “Boys Of The Lough”. McDonald would suggest Scottish origin, but that’s pure speculation on my part.

↳ Posted by Kenny on October 30th, 2004.

Miss McDonald

I’ve heard this played occasionally in sessions. A fine tune with a driving rhythm that deserves more exposure.
Trevor

↳ Posted by fidicen on April 2nd, 2005.

Miss McDonald, X:3

Here is the version which appears in O’Neill’s Dance Music of Ireland - 1001 Gems (1907), p. 93, no. 486, as Miss McDonald, Ingean Ní Mic Domnaill.

↳ Posted by Moxhe on October 27th, 2015.

The Spinning Wheel

This is a simplified setting of The Spinning Wheel in O’Neill’s 1001 (#479). Quite different from The Spinning Wheel at https://thesession.org/tunes/8570, though there are some similar phrases if they’re transposed to the same key (which I’ll post next). It’s heavy on the triplet runs, so I’ve pared that down.

Bill Black’s ABC simplified version at http://www.capeirish.com/webabc/working/source.folders/onmi1850/onmi_reels/onmi.reels_ABC.txt differs from the source in contour at a few bars, so I’ve tried to split the difference. He also transcribed the original with triplets.

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on December 31st, 2020.

The Spinning Wheel, X:5

Here’s a transposition down to D -- the first bar is similar to https://thesession.org/tunes/8570, but otherwise they might as well be different tunes entirely.

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on December 31st, 2020.

Re: The Spinning Wheel

This tune can be seen in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection as “Miss McDonald’s” in the key of G. Teada recorded it as “The Spinnign Wheel” on their 2013 album In Spite of the Storm. Ah, and according to https://thesession.org/tunes/3779 it’s in Dance Music of Ireland (1907) as “Miss McDonald”, No.486.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on January 1st, 2021.
